On the admissible record, certification is defensible only as a conditional or caveated action: aggregate readiness is supported by BMCARD-049-A, the small-business support slice weakness is established by BMCARD-049-B, BMCARD-049-C permits certification only if that weakness is explicitly disclosed or an approved mitigation removes exposure, BMCARD-049-D explains why follow-up confirmation is warranted, and BMCARD-049-E shows no approved mitigation is available. The correct interpretation is therefore not 'cleanly compliant certification now,' but 'certification is policy-consistent if and only if the final model card specifically discloses the unresolved slice weakness and its uncertainty.' That narrowing addresses the overbreadth concern without requiring escalation beyond a caveated compliance posture.

output.claims_about_policy: The policy text is conditional, not prohibitory. It allows certification when a material weakness is disclosed, even if unresolved, unless an approved mitigation instead removes exposure. The admissible record supports three policy conclusions: aggregate performance can support launch readiness but does not erase subgroup weakness; small-sample uncertainty can justify monitoring and prompt re-checks but cannot convert the case into clean certification; and the absence of an approved mitigation means disclosure is the only supported compliance path on this record. The audited claim should therefore be read as a caveated certification position contingent on explicit model-card disclosure, not as an assertion that aggregate performance alone makes certification compliant.
